newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-BOBEK SKATES ON DESPITE COACH'S DEATH.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-BOBEK SKATES ON DESPITE COACH'S DEATH.

text.p: Distraught Nicole Bobek has insisted she will compete in the world figure skating championships despite the death on Thursday of her coach Carlo Fassi from a heart attack at the age of 67.
Fassi also coached former Olympic champions Peggy Fleming and Dorothy Hamill of the United States and Britons John Curry and Robin Cousins.
Bobek, 19, was third in the 1995 world championships and third at last month's U.S. Nationals. Her event starts on Friday.
Wearing dark glasses, Bobek, issued a brief statement on Thursday before departing in tears.
"I'd just like to say what has happened today is a tragedy. It is very hard but we know he is here for all of us. We just can't see him," she said.
"He was always been there for me and always took the part of a father for me."
She said she would be supporting another of Fassi's skaters, Cornel Gheorghe of Romania, when he competed in the free skating on Thursday night.
"Robin Cousins...asked us if we wanted him (Cousins) to stand with me in the competition and we have agreed to that. It is hard for him as well. It is hard for all of us.
"From what I heard , one of Carlo's last words was to ask Christa (his wife and coaching partner) to please be with me during the competition.
"We all love him and we will miss him," she said.
"He had a history of hard work," Cousins, here as a television commentator, said. "There was no Carlo Fassi at half mast. It was all or nothing."
